content.title: About
content.content: Canned cherries (Cerasus) are whole cherries that have been blanched, pitted and packed in syrup or their own juice. They retain a sweet‑tart flavor, bright aroma and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are close relatives of sweet cherries and plums.
Canning allows cherries to be stored for 2‑3 years without loss of taste.
Cherries are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins, which give them their deep red color.
Traditional canning uses a sugar syrup, but sugar‑free versions also exist.
Canned cherries are commonly used in baking, desserts and sauces.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids in cherries may improve circulation and lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned cherries are low in fat and moderately caloric, making them suitable for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Most canned cherries contain added sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or those watching their sugar intake.

items.title: Cherry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may use preservatives such as sodium sorbate.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature can irritate a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned cherries can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to yogurt, oatmeal, salads, baked goods, sauces, and smoothies. They pair well with cottage cheese, ice cream and chocolate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if mold, off‑odor, or other signs of spoilage appear.
